t: A union of the Anglian kingdoms of Bernicia and Deira that stretched from the Humber to the Firth of Forth.
Its monasteries produced Bede, Alcuin, the Lindisfarne Gospels and the Codex Amiatinus, the Northumbrian Renaissance.
Defeat at Nechtansmere in 685 ended its expansion; the Vikings took York in 867 and England absorbed it in 954.
dyk: The Codex Amiatinus, made at Wearmouth-Jarrow and the oldest surviving complete Latin Bible, was long thought to be Italian until its Northumbrian origin was identified in the 1880s.
ev: Oswiu defeats and kills Penda of Mercia at the Battle of the Winwaed
The Synod of Whitby adopts Roman practice for dating Easter
The Picts defeat and kill Ecgfrith at the Battle of Nechtansmere
Bede completes the Ecclesiastical History of the English People
Vikings sack the monastery of Lindisfarne
The Great Heathen Army holds York; kings Osberht and Ælla are killed
Eric Bloodaxe is expelled and Northumbria passes to the English crown

f.predecessor: Kingdom of Bernicia; Kingdom of Deira
f.successor: Kingdom of York; Earldom of Bamburgh; Kingdom of England
